records.text: And I filled up My fury and held back and did not bring them to an end. I will pour it upon little children outside and upon a gathering of young men together, because man and woman will be seized, the elder with one full of days.
For from their small to their great, all have carried out lawless deeds; from priest to false prophet, all have done false things.
And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?

They were put to shame because they failed, and even so they were not at all ashamed and did not recognize their dishonor. Therefore they will fall in their fall, and at the time of their visitation they will perish, said the Lord.
Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, called as an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
which He promised beforehand through His prophets in holy Scriptures,
concerning His Son, who came from David’s seed according to the flesh,
who was designated Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
through whom we received grace and apostleship for the obedience of faith among all the nations for His name,
among whom you also are, called by Jesus Christ:
to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called as saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Then Job replied:
“How long will you weary my soul and tear me down with words?
Know only that the Lord made me like this. You speak against me; without shame you press upon me.
Yes, indeed, I truly went astray, and error lodges with me—
to speak a word that ought not have been spoken; my words wander and are not timely.
But leave off magnifying yourselves against me and leaping upon me with reproach.
Know, then, that the Lord is the One who disturbed me and raised His stronghold against me.
Behold, I laugh in reproach and will not speak; I will cry out, but judgment is nowhere.
I have been walled in all around and cannot pass through; He placed darkness before my face.
He tore me apart all around, and I was gone; He cut off my hope like a tree.
He dealt with me terribly in anger and regarded me like an enemy.
His trials came together against me on my roads; men lying in wait encircled me.
My brothers withdrew from me; they recognized strangers rather than me, and my friends became merciless.
Those nearest me did not acknowledge me, and those who knew my name forgot me.
I called my servant, but he did not answer; my mouth made entreaty.
I entreated my wife and called with flattering words to the sons of my concubines.
They disowned me for ever; whenever I rise, they speak against me.
Those who knew me abhorred me; those I had loved rose against me.
They humiliated women in Zion, virgins in Judah’s cities.
Rulers were hung by their hands; elders were not glorified.
Chosen men took up weeping, and young men weakened under wood.
Elders ceased from the gate, chosen men ceased from their songs.
The joy of our heart ended; our dancing turned to mourning.
For this our heart became sorrowful; for this our eyes grew dim,
because Mount Zion was destroyed; foxes passed through her.
God, Thou knewest my folly, and my offenses were not concealed from Thee.
May those waiting for Thee not be ashamed because of me, Lord, Lord of powers; may those seeking Thee not be embarrassed because of me, God of Israel,
for on Thine account I endured reproach; embarrassment covered my face.
for zeal for Thy house devoured me, and the reproaches of those reproaching Thee fell upon me.
I bowed my soul down in fasting, and it became a reproach to me.
I made sackcloth my garment, and became a proverb to them.
Those sitting in the gate talked against me, and wine-drinkers sang about me.
Then Zophar the Minaean replied:
“I did not expect you to answer back like this, and you all do not understand more than I do.
I will hear correction that puts me to shame, and a spirit from understanding answers me.
Did you not know these things from long ago, since a human was placed upon the earth?
For the delight of the ungodly is a terrible fall, and the joy of the lawless is destruction,
He will certainly not be saved from the hand of iron; may a bronze bow wound him.
May an arrow pass through his body, and may lightning bolts walk among his dwellings; terrors are upon him.
May every darkness remain for him; an unkindled fire will consume him, and may a stranger harm his house.
May heaven uncover his lawless deeds, and may earth rise against him.
This is an ungodly person’s portion from the Lord, and the possession of his belongings from the Overseer.”
An unjust thought is an abomination to the Lord, but the sayings of pure people are noble.
One who takes bribes destroys himself, but one who hates taking gifts is saved.
By acts of mercy and faithfulness sins are thoroughly cleansed, and by the fear of the Lord everyone turns from evil.
The hearts of the righteous meditate on faithful things, but the mouth of the impious answers evil things.
The ways of righteous men are acceptable to the Lord, and through them even enemies become friends.
God is far distant from the impious, but He listens to the prayers of the righteous.
